title: HostedAPI ephemeral stream jitter - field notes and runbook draft
content:
Executive summary:

On 2027-09-29 04:12 UTC we observed a cross-region degradation impacting a subset of Hosted API streaming sessions: user-visible output stalls, elevated per-request tail latency, and intermittent 5xx for stream-resume operations. The impact window lasted ~26 minutes for affected customers before mitigation. Approximately 8% of streaming sessions across EU-west and us-central showed degraded progress (stalled bytes or repeated reconnects).

What happened (short):
- A change deployed three days earlier to the session-resume backoff logic inadvertently enabled rapid reconnect retries when partial KV-cache entries were present.
- On session reconnect, the resume path attempted aggressive KV prefetch and parallelized warmup (to reduce LLM cold-start tokens). When many sessions resumed simultaneously (normal morning traffic pattern + region failover handoffs), this created short bursts of heavy KV cache mutations and lease churn.
- The KV lease churn caused transient increases in lock latency and a small percentage of session resume RPCs to time out and surface as 5xx to clients.
- Downstream, the streaming multiplexer retry timer had a subtle bug that triggered duplicate resume attempts for in-flight reconnects, amplifying the load by ~1.6x.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: streaming stalls (no tokens emitted for 2–10s) and occasional connection resets for affected sessions. Some interactive UIs retried and exposed spinner freeze to end-users.
- Scope: ~8% of streaming sessions in two regions, affecting ~120 customer orgs (mostly mid-market PLG tiers). No data loss observed.
- Severity: P0 (availability degradation for subset of traffic).

Detection and metrics: 
- Alerting: the anomaly was first flagged by the streaming-progress-slo-alert (end-to-end token throughput drop in region) and by on-call SRE via elevated error budget burn.
- Useful signals: session_resume_latency_p50/p95, kv_cache_lease_ops_per_sec, kv_lock_wait_ms, streaming_multiplexer_retries, backend_5xx_rate_by_path.
- Breadcrumbs seen in logs: repeated resume attempts within 500ms windows, KV lease renewals flapping, RPC timeouts at the resume RPC (deadline exceeded).

Timeline (UTC):
- 04:09: deploy rolled 2027-09-26 to stage and production (resume-backoff tweak, parallel prefetch). No immediate regressions observed.
- 04:11: morning traffic ramp in EU-west; first anomalies in telemetry.
- 04:12: streaming-progress-slo alert fired (on-call pager).
- 04:13: SRE on-call triaged, found session_resume_latency_p95 spike and elevated kv_lock_wait_ms.
- 04:14–04:20: engineering joined (runtime + kv team). Quick hypothesis: prefetch + parallelization causing KV pressure.
- 04:21: short-term mitigation (manual config flip): disable aggressive parallel prefetch for resume path via feature flag.
- 04:23: multiplexer retry backoff applied (kill-switch for duplicate resume condition) in the edge tier.
- 04:25: error rates fell, token throughput recovered towards baseline.
- 04:38: incident declared resolved for customer impact; monitoring kept open for regression.

Root cause analysis (evidence-backed):
- Primary cause: change to resume path enabling parallel prefetch of KV prefixes combined with no cap on parallelism. This produced transient KV server overload (lease churn and lock contention). Metric: kv_cache_lease_ops_per_sec spiked 3.2x relative to baseline immediately preceding the incident window.
- Secondary amplification: streaming multiplexer duplicate-resume bug (race condition) caused some reconnect flows to perform two resume attempts concurrently. Reproduce locally with interleaved pause/resume test harness: PR linked.
- Contributing factor: autoscaler headroom in one of the KV clusters was low (recent packing optimization) so short bursts triggered queuing delays rather than absorbing load.

Why the safeguards didn't block this:
- The feature flag for parallel prefetch was enabled in prod because stage telemetry looked benign - stage traffic didn't exercise the same session-resume fan-in patterns.
- There was no quota/circuit-breaker in resume path that would have limited per-session parallel prefetch.
- Multiplexer invariant tests did not cover the specific interleaving that produced duplicate resumes; test suite gap.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Disabled parallel prefetch feature flag for resume path (prod).
- Applied a server-side knob to cap resume parallelism to 1 for affected regions.
- Hotfix to the multiplexer: added a guard to dedupe in-flight resume operations (edge-config kill-switch). Deployed as emergency patch.
- Increased KV cluster autoscaler target by 15% for the impacted pool to give short-term headroom.

Longer-term action items (owners & ETA):
- RE-1427: Add per-session parallelism quota and back-pressure for resume prefetch. Owner: Jonas Kim. ETA: 2027-10-14.
- RE-1430: Permanent fix for multiplexer duplicate-resume race (PR and integration test). Owner: Maya Ruiz. ETA: 2027-10-07.
- RE-1435: Add chaos/canary test for session-resume fan-in patterns (simulated region failover/connect storms). Owner: Eng QA. ETA: 2027-10-21.
- SRE-ops-58: Autoscaler tuning and comfortable headroom policy for KV pools servicing resume/prewarm traffic. Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2027-10-05.
- RE-1442: Observability: add a composite alert that correlates resume latency + kv_lease_churn + retry amplification metric to reduce detection-to-page time. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2027-10-03.

Runbook draft for future P0 (Streaming session resume jitter):
- Detection triggers: session_resume_latency_p95 > 1.5x baseline for >5m OR streaming_progress_rate drop >20% for >3m combined with backend_5xx_rate_by_path >0.5%
- Immediate checklist for on-call SRE:
  1) Annotate incident and start timeline in shared doc.
  2) Check session_resume_parallelism_flag state across regions. If enabled and recent change: toggle off (feature-flag UI).
  3) Inspect kv_cache_lease_ops_per_sec and kv_lock_wait_ms; if >2x baseline, increase KV autoscaler target for the affected pool (temporary +15%).
  4) Flip multiplexer duplicate-resume kill-switch (edge tier) if retries amplification shows >1.2x.
  5) If 5xx persists after steps 2–4, escalate to runtime lead and consider full traffic failover to fallback-tier model for streaming path.
  6) Communicate with CS/Support with templated status update: short summary, mitigation steps, ETA for follow-up.

Telemetry and test gaps discovered: 
- Missing test coverage for resume multiplexer race interleavings.
- No synthetic canary that simulates large-scale simultaneous resume fan-in; stage load profile didn't match prod pattern.
- Lack of a per-resume parallelism metric surfaced late; add instrumentation.

Post-incident notes from on-call (raw):
- "04:13: felt like we were seeing repeated resumes very quickly — logs had same session-id twice within 300ms." — on-call
- "Feature flag had been flipped cluster-wide 72h earlier; stage didn't show it because stage sessions are shorter on average" — runtime eng
- "KV pool scaling needs a safety buffer if packing changes go in — we almost always see regressions when headroom is tight" — infra

Customer comms snapshot (for CS):
- Short: "We saw transient streaming stalls and reconnects for a portion of streaming sessions in EU and us-central due to resume-path performance issues. We removed the aggressive resume prefetch and applied a hotfix; service is recovered. We're doing follow-up work to prevent recurrence and will share a technical summary."

Appendix: quick reproduction steps (internal):
1) Use stress harness with 5k simulated sessions, create bursty reconnect of 15% of sessions at t=0.
2) Enable parallel prefetch flag.
3) Observe kv_cache_lease_ops_per_sec spike and streaming_multiplexer_retries amplification >1.4x.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should prefetch be default-disabled and opt-in? (risk/cost tradeoff).
- Do we need a dedicated small, fast KV tier for resume prewarm paths? Cost implications to evaluate.

Summary takeaway:
The incident was caused by an optimistic optimization (parallel resume prefetch) that did not account for prod-scale fan-in and was amplified by a separate retry-race in the multiplexer. The immediate mitigations succeeded; the long-term fixes are reasonable and time-bound. This event highlights the importance of canary shapes matching prod fan-in, stronger per-flow safeguards, and targeted integration tests for resume flows.

Document history / notes:
- Drafted by Aisha Patel (SRE lead) with runtime and KV team input.
- Will convert into formal postmortem after long-term fixes land and we validate tests and alerts.
summary: Field notes covering a P0-scale streaming session resume jitter incident: root cause, timeline, mitigations, runbook draft, and action items.
